selected_evidence.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
selected_evidence.summary: Initial cert (serial=1000, notAfter 03:24:35) issued by renew-cert.sh; cert-renew.timer enabled and firing every 30s; at 03:22:00 (before the 03:24:35 expiry) the timer-triggered service automatically renewed the cert to serial=1001 with new notAfter 03:28:00, confirmed via journalctl log entry and openssl x509 output

selected_evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime during rotation)
selected_evidence.summary: A 2-second polling probe against https://node1:8443 spanning the 03:22:00 renewal logged serial flipping from 1000 to 1001 mid-stream with 85/85 requests returning http_code=200 and 0 failures, proving nginx's `systemctl reload` picked up the new cert without dropping traffic

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before reboot
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc, uptime since 23:15:29, nginx and cert-renew.timer active, valid cert serial=1001, and HTTPS returning 200 immediately before triggering reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: reboot acknowledgement returns before disconnect, then node becomes reachable again with changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command backgrounded with a short delay so its ack returned before the connection dropped; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset/timeout while node1 was down; polling succeeded once it came back, showing a new boot_id=c736699c-ee12-4dd9-9411-4dfb945094ad and fresh uptime start of 23:22:31, proving an actual restart occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required services and automation, including a subsequent automatic renewal proving persistence
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, nginx and cert-renew.timer are both active and enabled, firewall port 8443 persisted, and HTTPS returns 200 again; the timer resumed its schedule and, without any manual intervention, performed a second live renewal (serial 1001->1002, notAfter extended to 03:31:20) while HTTPS continued returning 200, confirming the auto-renewal setup survives a reboot
